main.title: Gears of War
main.subtitle: The Weight of Moving Forward Together
main.summary: Epic Games builds Gears of War around cover, cooperative advances and a reload that rewards precise timing.

cards.heading: Marcus and the Locust
cards.text: Epic Games released Gears of War for Xbox 360 on November 7, 2006 in North America. Marcus Fenix and his squad fight the Locust through ruined cities, moving from cover to cover under fire. The campaign supports two players, while competitive modes bring the same heavy movement and close-range weapons to compact arenas. Unreal Engine 3 gives the characters, lighting and scarred architecture a distinctive appearance.

cards.heading: Moving between cover
cards.text: The A button brings several movements together: taking cover, moving to another position, vaulting an obstacle and beginning the crouched Roadie Run. A wall protects the player from one direction but can leave a flank exposed. Moving forward means choosing the next position and checking the route to it. The camera stays close to Marcus, emphasizing the weight and limited view of each advance.

cards.heading: Active Reload
cards.text: Active Reload adds a timing challenge while the weapon is being refilled. Pressing the reload command again stops a moving indicator: a well-timed attempt shortens the wait and can grant an additional advantage, while a mistake leaves the player vulnerable for longer. The decision takes place during the firefight, when an enemy may be closing the distance.

cards.heading: Marcus and Dom
cards.text: Marcus and Dom can be controlled by two players on the same console or through Xbox Live. Some sections separate their paths before bringing them together again. One player can draw attention while the other moves around an enemy or protects a flank. In a solo campaign, artificial intelligence controls Dom, keeping the partnership present throughout the journey.

cards.heading: The Lancer
cards.text: The Lancer combines an assault rifle with a chainsaw bayonet. It supports firing from cover at medium range, then gives a much more forceful option when an enemy comes close. Using the chainsaw requires an approach that can expose the player to other attackers. Its sound, animation and vibration match the heavy movement of the characters and make the weapon immediately recognizable.

cards.heading: Unreal Engine 3
cards.text: Epic developed Gears of War alongside Unreal Engine 3, demonstrating the technology in a full Xbox 360 game. Detailed character models, damaged surfaces and lighting showed other developers what the engine could produce. The game also served as an example of the tools Epic offered to other studios, linking its visual influence to the spread of the engine.

cards.heading: Cover against human opponents
cards.text: Human opponents change how cover is used. They can flank, anticipate a move or tempt a player to leave a protected position. Small teams and compact maps keep these encounters concentrated, while modes without respawns make each loss costly. Roadie Run, Active Reload and the weapons remain familiar from the campaign, but their timing must now account for another player's decisions.

main.title: Elite Beat Agents
main.subtitle: Help arrives on the beat
main.summary: Elite Beat Agents is iNiS's Nintendo DS rhythm game about a secret team sent to encourage people through moments of crisis. Commander Kahn dispatches the dancing agents into a series of comic-book situations, from everyday troubles to increasingly extravagant emergencies. The player follows popular songs through tapping, dragging and spinning actions on the touchscreen. Made as an international counterpart to Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan, it replaces that game's Japanese setting and music with a new cast, stories and licensed songs recorded as in-game covers.

cards.heading: An action for each musical phrase
cards.text: Numbered circles appear across the lower screen, with closing rings indicating when to tap. Other patterns ask the stylus to follow a moving marker or spin repeatedly. The upper screen shows the current story and the agents' encouragement, letting musical performance alter how the situation develops. The player has to listen as well as follow the visual sequence. A familiar song provides a structure to anticipate, while the changing placement of targets turns that structure into a small physical routine performed with the hand.

cards.heading: A good performance changes the story
cards.text: The short stories give a missed beat an immediate comic consequence: the person being helped can struggle or recover as the performance changes. That feedback ties a scoring challenge to a visible reason for playing well. Different difficulty levels rearrange the demands of a song, allowing an already familiar scene to support another attempt. Elite Beat Agents makes its encouragement unusually generous. The spectacle belongs to the characters above, but the repeated, precise gestures below are what allow their unlikely rescue to keep moving.

main.title: Viva Piñata
main.subtitle: A garden with a life of its own
main.summary: Viva Piñata is Rare's garden simulation for Xbox 360, released in 2006. Its animals are living piñatas, attracted by the plants, water and other creatures around them. Starting with a neglected plot and a few tools, the player gradually builds a place where new species can visit and make their home.

cards.heading: An invitation to Piñata Island
cards.text: Viva Piñata is Rare's garden simulation for Xbox 360, released in 2006. Its animals are living piñatas, attracted by the plants, water and other creatures around them. Starting with a neglected plot and a few tools, the player gradually builds a place where new species can visit and make their home.

cards.heading: Making room for a visitor
cards.text: Clear ground with the shovel, sow seeds and keep the plants watered. These changes create conditions that particular piñatas need: a patch of grass, a certain flower or a suitable neighbour can bring a new visitor to the edge of the garden. Checking its information reveals what would persuade it to stay.

cards.heading: A place to settle
cards.text: A wild piñata gains its full colours when it becomes a resident. Give it a name, build a house and meet the conditions for a pair to romance. Their dance leads to an egg delivered by Storkos. Different diets can also reveal colour variants, rewarding experiments with the inhabitants already living nearby.

cards.heading: Looking after the garden
cards.text: The garden keeps developing while its owner tends another corner. Plants need attention, rivals can fight, and Sour piñatas bring trouble. Helpers can take over chores such as watering or gathering produce. Each decision changes the balance of the plot: a new arrival may need the very plant or creature that another resident depends on.

main.title: PlayStation 3
main.subtitle: The console becomes a connected place
main.summary: Blu-ray discs, a hard drive and PlayStation Network brought games, films and an expanding online world into one machine.

cards.heading: Sony's seventh-generation home console
cards.text: The PlayStation 3 (PS3) is a home video game console developed and marketed by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). It is the successor to the PlayStation 2, and both are part of the PlayStation brand of consoles. It competed primarily with Microsoft's Xbox 360 and Nintendo's Wii as part of the seventh generation of video game consoles.

cards.heading: Blu-ray and the connected dashboard
cards.text: Sony's ambition extended beyond a faster games console. A Blu-ray drive offered another way to watch high-definition films, while a hard drive and PlayStation Network supported downloadable games and online services. The XrossMediaBar organised this growing collection of activities into rows of icons. The machine could be a disc player, a meeting point and a game library, sometimes in the same evening.

cards.heading: Different games on a shared platform
cards.text: That wider role did not give the generation just one creative direction. Resistance explored a large-scale shooter, Uncharted built an adventure around characters and spectacle, and LittleBigPlanet invited players to make and share levels. The large, curved original console displayed here belongs to the beginning of that story. Smaller redesigns arrived in 2009 and 2012.

main.title: Resistance: Fall of Man
main.summary: Nathan Hale fights through an occupied Britain with weapons whose secondary fire changes how cover and movement work.

cards.heading: Resistance: Fall of Man
cards.text: Resistance: Fall of Man introduced Insomniac Games' first-person shooter series at the Japanese PlayStation 3 launch in November 2006. Set in an alternative 1951, it follows American soldier Nathan Hale through a Britain overrun by the Chimera. Military streets and alien machinery share the campaign, alongside weapons with unusually adaptable secondary fire.

cards.heading: Give the bullets an address
cards.text: The Bullseye gives a burst of fire a destination. Attach its secondary-fire tag to an enemy and subsequent rounds bend towards that point, letting Hale move while continuing the attack. The first accurate hit changes what follows: attention can shift from keeping the target in the sights to finding a safer position. Other weapons offer their own paired functions, so choosing a gun also means choosing how to prepare the next few seconds of combat.

cards.heading: Cover with a weakness
cards.text: A barricade offers little comfort when a Steelhead carries an Auger. Its shots pass through solid surfaces, making a position that stopped ordinary bullets suddenly dangerous. Hale can use the same weapon, with secondary fire creating a temporary energy shield. The encounter asks for more than a quick exchange of shots: identify the weapon across the street, decide whether the wall still helps and change position before the incoming rounds reach it.

cards.heading: A familiar country under occupation
cards.text: The campaign moves through British towns and cities, where terraces, churches and railway spaces stand beside the Chimera's conversion facilities. Following human troops into a street establishes a familiar scale; meeting a large alien machine changes it immediately. The contrast carries through the equipment, from a carbine with an underslung grenade launcher to captured energy weapons. Each advance brings the invading technology closer, making the country feel progressively occupied as Hale approaches the enemy's installations.

main.title: Ridge Racer 7
main.summary: Ridge Racer 7 is a 2006 racing video game developed and published by Namco Bandai Games for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: Ridge Racer joins the PlayStation 3 launch
cards.text: Ridge Racer 7 brought Namco Bandai's racing series to the PlayStation 3 launch in 2006. It followed Ridge Racer 6 on Xbox 360, carrying familiar cars and courses into a new edition with additional content.

cards.heading: Forty cars and twenty-two courses
cards.text: The game has around 40 cars, many of which are from Ridge Racer 6 and Ridge Racer (PSP). There are also 22 courses, available in forward, reverse and mirrored. The game runs at 1080p native resolution and 60 frames per second. It also features Dolby Digital 5.1 surround sound and free online gameplay via the PlayStation Network. Like many other Ridge Racer games, it features a full motion video opening that stars mascot Reiko Nagase.

cards.heading: A later patch adds 3 D play
cards.text: The game received positive reviews from critics. A patch was made available in October 2010 titled Ridge Racer 7 3D License Version that enables Ridge Racer 7 to be played in 3D. Following this, Bugbear developed the drastically different Ridge Racer Unbounded, released in 2012.

main.title: Yoshi's Island DS
main.subtitle: More babies for the journey
main.summary: Yoshi's Island DS is Artoon's Nintendo DS platform game following the Yoshis as they rescue children kidnapped by Kamek. It extends the Super Nintendo adventure's hand-drawn appearance, egg throwing and flutter jumps across both handheld displays. The major addition is a group of babies with different abilities. Choosing who rides on Yoshi's back can change the route through a level. The rescue gives the familiar travelling partnership several new forms, letting a companion's particular skill become the key to reaching the next platform or hidden object.

cards.heading: More babies for the journey
cards.text: Yoshi's Island DS is Artoon's Nintendo DS platform game following the Yoshis as they rescue children kidnapped by Kamek. It extends the Super Nintendo adventure's hand-drawn appearance, egg throwing and flutter jumps across both handheld displays. The major addition is a group of babies with different abilities. Choosing who rides on Yoshi's back can change the route through a level. The rescue gives the familiar travelling partnership several new forms, letting a companion's particular skill become the key to reaching the next platform or hidden object.

cards.heading: A different passenger, another route
cards.text: Baby Mario allows Yoshi to dash and reveal particular blocks, while Baby Peach's parasol helps him ride air currents. Baby Donkey Kong can grip vines and ropes, Baby Wario attracts metal objects with a magnet, and Baby Bowser breathes fire. Switching at the appropriate places turns the cast into a set of tools for exploration. A section that looks inaccessible with one passenger can make sense with another. The player needs to understand both Yoshi's shared movement and the extra possibility supplied by the baby currently being carried.

cards.heading: Recover the child before time runs out
cards.text: Yoshi can swallow enemies, turn them into eggs and aim those eggs at distant targets or switches. A hit separates him from his passenger, starting a countdown in which the baby must be recovered. That interruption makes protection a physical task inside the level rather than only a reduction in health. The tall playing area gives movement another scale, with the gap between screens becoming something to judge carefully. The familiar actions still anchor the adventure while its expanded cast supplies reasons to reconsider how a level can be crossed.

main.title: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
main.subtitle: Two visitors to Dracula's castle
main.summary: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is Konami's Nintendo DS action role-playing game set in Europe during the Second World War. Jonathan Morris and Charlotte Aulin investigate a castle whose paintings lead into other locations. Jonathan brings physical combat skills, while Charlotte specialises in magic. Their partnership gives the adventure two distinct ways to approach an enemy or obstacle. The castle remains the centre of an interconnected journey, but the paintings allow it to open onto environments that are visually and geographically different from its own rooms.

Their partnership gives the adventure two distinct ways to approach an enemy or obstacle. The castle remains the centre of an interconnected journey, but the paintings allow it to open onto environments that are visually and geographically different from its own rooms.

cards.heading: Call the partner you need
cards.text: The player can switch between Jonathan and Charlotte or call the other character into action as a partner. Their different abilities make the choice useful beyond the appearance of the next attack. Combined techniques encourage the pair to work together, while particular obstacles require their skills in the right arrangement. Equipment and experience continue to support the role-playing progression. Instead of replacing one protagonist with another for an entire chapter, Portrait of Ruin makes their relationship available as an ordinary decision throughout movement, exploration and fighting.

cards.heading: A picture becomes a destination
cards.text: The paintings interrupt the castle's familiar architecture with places such as an Egyptian desert and a town inspired by London. Entering one changes the setting without abandoning the larger investigation. Returning to the castle then restores a shared point of reference for the journey. The game also introduces a separate cooperative mode through online play, extending the idea of a pair beyond its story characters. Its most distinctive contribution remains the accessible partnership: two complementary people can occupy the centre of a Castlevania adventure at once.

main.title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
main.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess is a 2006 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the GameCube and Wii.

cards.heading: A Zelda adventure spans two Nintendo consoles
cards.text: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess is a 2006 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the GameCube and Wii. Originally planned for release exclusively on the GameCube in November 2005, Nintendo delayed the release to refine the game, add more content and port it to the Wii. The Wii version was a launch game in North America in November 2006 and in Japan, Europe and Australia the following month. The GameCube version was released in December 2006 as the final first-party game for the console.

cards.heading: Link, Midna and the Twilight Realm
cards.text: The game takes place over a century after Majora's Mask, in an alternate timeline from The Wind Waker. Players control Link, who tries to prevent Hyrule from being engulfed by a corrupted parallel dimension, the Twilight Realm. He takes the form of both a Hylian and a wolf and is assisted by a mysterious imp named Midna.

cards.heading: Reception and the Wii U remaster
cards.text: Twilight Princess received critical acclaim, with praise for its art direction, combat, level design and story. It received numerous game of the year awards, and has been called one of the greatest video games ever made. By 2015, it had sold 8.85 million copies worldwide, making it the best-selling Zelda game until Breath of the Wild (2017). In 2011, the Wii version was rereleased under the Nintendo Selects label. A high-definition remaster based on the GameCube version, The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD, developed by Tantalus Media and Nintendo EPD, was released for the Wii U in March 2016. An eleven-volume manga series based on Twilight Princess by Akira Himekawa was published between 2016 and 2022.

main.title: Wii Sports
main.summary: Wii Sports is a 2006 sports simulation video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii video game console.

cards.text: Wii Sports is a 2006 sports simulation video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii video game console. The game was released in North America along with the Wii on 19 November 2006, and in Japan, Australia, and Europe the following month. It was included as a pack-in game with the console in all territories except Japan and Korea, making it the first sports game included with the launch of a Nintendo system since Mario's Tennis for the Virtual Boy in 1995. The game was later released on its own as part of the Nintendo Selects collection of games.

Wii Sports is a collection of five sports simulations designed to demonstrate the motion-sensing capabilities of the Wii Remote. The five sports included are tennis, baseball, bowling, golf, and boxing. Players use the Wii Remote to mimic actions performed in real-life sports, such as swinging a tennis racket or rolling a bowling ball. The rules for each game are simplified to make them more accessible to new players. The game also features training and fitness modes that monitor players' progress in the sports.

Wii Sports reached a large audience through its inclusion with the console and sold 82 million copies worldwide. Critics and players responded warmly to the collection. Television coverage, commercials and organised competitions helped make its familiar gestures recognisable beyond the usual games audience. Shared play also gave people of different ages a reason to gather around the same screen.

On 25 June 2009, a sequel, Wii Sports Resort, was released, which contained 12 sports, 10 of which were not seen in the original. A high-definition (HD) remake of Wii Sports titled Wii Sports Club was released on 11 July 2014 for the Wii U. Another sequel, Nintendo Switch Sports, was released for the Nintendo Switch on 29 April 2022.
